questions.q: When is a @TestSetup method's data rolled back?
options: After every individual test method in the class finishes
Once, at the end of the entire test class's execution — though any per-method changes to it roll back after that method
Never — @TestSetup data persists permanently in the org
Only when the test class is deleted
questions.explain: Data created in @TestSetup rolls back once at the end of the whole class's run, but if an individual test method modifies that shared data, those changes roll back after that method so the next method sees the original state.

questions.q: How many @TestSetup methods can a single test class have?
options: Unlimited
Up to five
Exactly one
One per test method in the class
questions.explain: A test class is limited to a single @TestSetup method, which runs before every test method in that class.

questions.q: Which of the following is true about combining @TestSetup with @isTest(SeeAllData=true)?
options: They work together seamlessly in any API version
@TestSetup methods are not supported in a class or method using SeeAllData=true
SeeAllData=true is required in order to use @TestSetup
Using both together doubles the available governor limits
questions.explain: @TestSetup depends on the default data isolation mode; it is not supported in a class or test method marked @isTest(SeeAllData=true).

questions.q: A developer notices they're writing if/else logic inside a @TestSetup method to create different data for different test methods. What does this usually indicate?
options: This is the recommended pattern for all @TestSetup methods
The data isn't actually shared across methods and probably belongs in each method or a direct factory call instead
The test class has too many test methods and should be split in two
@TestSetup methods cannot contain conditional logic at all and this will fail to compile
questions.explain: If different test methods need meaningfully different setup data, that data isn't truly shared baseline data — it's a sign the setup should move into the individual test methods or a direct factory call instead.

questions.q: What is the method signature requirement for a @TestSetup method?
options: It must be an instance method that accepts a List<SObject> argument
It must be static, take no arguments, and return no value
It must return a Boolean indicating success
It must be marked @AuraEnabled as well as @TestSetup
questions.explain: A @TestSetup method must be static, take no arguments, and return no value — the same basic shape as an @isTest method.
